newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 2.00 cents per lb lower on Wednesday, in a technical correction to the market's recent sharp run-up, traders said.
However, some traders doubted the market would make its due, saying prices were likely to come in closer to unchanged as sentiment remained bullish.
"There was no selling yesterday," said one dealer, "and I don't anticipate there being any today."
Tuesday, New York arabica futures rallied for the second day in a row, bolstered by speculative buying amid bullish technicals and concerns about tight nearby supply.

September surged 9.35 cents, to a fresh eight-week high of 203.10 cents, after trading from 204.50 to 192.00. December rose 6.00 cents, to 174.70 cents, while the back months closed 1.95 to 3.70 cents higher.
The September/December switch, a barometer of near-term availability, bulged to 28.40 cents compared with 25.05 cents at the close on Monday.
Technically, September support was pegged at 198.00 cents, while resistance was seen at 206.00 cents, traders said.
On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Wednesday that no damaging cold weather is expected during the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt.
After Tuesday's close the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 1,344 60-kg bags as of August 4, to 93,397 bags. An additional 4,679 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

Also after Tuesday's close, Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation said it was closing August registrations for federation and private coffee exports on August 8 at 1900 local/2400 GMT and opening all September coffee registrations on August 11.
In a statement, the federation confirmed it would maintain the 0.30 cent premium on Colombian coffee.

London robusta futures were firmer early Wednesday, lifted by trade and industry buying. At the midday break, September was up $9, to $1,665, after ranging from $1,678 to $1,664. November rose $14, to $1,669.
